query: CDW's revenue recognition: criteria for hardware vs. software vs. services.
final_answer: CDW applies different revenue recognition criteria for hardware, software, and services: Hardware - Revenue is recognized on a gross basis (as principal) when control passes to the customer, usually upon delivery, based on shipping terms in the contract. - For drop-shipment arrangements, CDW is still considered principal and recognizes revenue on a gross basis upon delivery to the customer. - In bill-and-hold arrangements, control passes when the hardware is ready for delivery, subject to criteria such as having a signed agreement, transfer of significant risks and rewards, customer’s ability to direct use, hardware being specifically set aside, and completion of any required configuration services (Chunks 2, 4, 7). Software - For perpetual and term licenses, if CDW acts as principal, revenue is recognized on a gross basis at the point the software is delivered (usually via electronic delivery of keys). - For software assurance sold with a license, if it is critical to the core functionality, it is combined as a single performance obligation. If not, software assurance is treated as a separate performance obligation and recognized on a net basis. - For cloud solutions (SaaS, IaaS) and most enterprise agreement (EA) transactions, CDW acts as agent and recognizes revenue on a net basis once its agency obligation is complete—typically at the point of sale or when the third-party vendor transfers the license and invoices the customer (Chunks 1, 4, 6, 8). Services - Professional services (e.g., project management, IT consulting) are recognized on a gross basis over time, using either time and materials for variable contracts or proportionally as costs are incurred for fixed-fee contracts (input method). - Hosted and managed services are recognized on a gross basis, ratably over the contractual term as stand-ready obligations. - For vendor partner delivered services (e.g., extended warranties), CDW acts as agent and recognizes revenue on a net basis at the point of sale, as these are considered separate performance obligations from the underlying product (Chunks 3, 6, 8). Bundled Arrangements - When hardware, software, and/or services are bundled, revenue is allocated to each distinct performance obligation based on their standalone selling prices (Chunks 3, 12). In summary: Hardware revenue is generally recognized upon delivery; software revenue depends on whether CDW is principal or agent and the nature of the software; and services revenue is recognized over time or at the point of sale depending on the type and whether CDW is principal or agent.

If the actual coupon redemption rate deviates from the estimated rate used to set reserves, this can impact the P&L in future periods. Conversely, if the redemption rate is lower, previously accrued reserves may be reversed, increasing net sales and profits. On cash flow, coupon reserve adjustments do not immediately affect cash, as cash outflows occur when coupons are actually redeemed and paid. However, changes in the reserve only impact cash flow if they result in higher or lower cash payments for coupon redemptions compared to accruals. Thus, variances between estimated and actual redemptions primarily affect the P&L, while the cash flow impact is realized as redemptions are paid out over time. In summary: - Coupon reserves reduce net sales and profit when accrued. - Redemption variances can lead to future P&L adjustments (either up or down). - Cash flow is affected only when actual coupon redemptions are paid, not when reserves are accrued or adjusted (Chunks 5, 6, 14).
